title: Poha (Flattened Rice Breakfast)
description: A quick and light Indian breakfast made with flattened rice, onions, and spices.
steps: Wash the poha in a colander under running water until just softened. Do not soak. Set aside.
Heat oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Add curry leaves and green chillies. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add finely chopped onions and cook until translucent, about 3–4 minutes.
Add turmeric powder and salt. Mix well.
Add the drained poha and gently mix without breaking the flakes.
Cook on low heat for 2–3 minutes, stirring gently.
Squeeze lemon juice and garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot.

title: Dal Rice (Red Lentil Dal with Steamed Rice)
description: Simple everyday dal made with red lentils and basic spices, served over steamed rice.
steps: Wash and soak red lentils for 15 minutes. Wash rice separately.
Pressure cook or boil lentils with 2 cups water, turmeric, and a pinch of salt until very soft.
Separately cook rice with 2 cups water until done.
Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let splutter.
Add finely chopped onions and fry until golden, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes, red chilli powder and coriander powder. Cook until tomatoes are soft.
Add the boiled lentils to the pan. Mix well and simmer for 5 minutes.
Adjust salt and consistency with water if needed. Serve hot over rice.

title: Egg Bhurji (Indian Scrambled Eggs)
description: Spiced Indian scrambled eggs cooked with onions, tomatoes and green chillies.
steps: Beat eggs with a pinch of salt and set aside.
Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add finely chopped onions and green chilli. Cook until onions are soft and lightly golden.
Add minced ginger, turmeric powder and red chilli powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add finely chopped tomatoes and cook until mushy, about 3 minutes.
Pour in beaten eggs. Do not stir immediately — wait 30 seconds.
Gently scramble the eggs with the masala using a spatula.
Cook until eggs are just set (slightly moist is better than dry).
Garnish with fresh coriander. Serve with bread or roti.

title: Besan Chilla (Chickpea Flour Pancakes)
description: Crispy savoury pancakes made from chickpea flour, great for breakfast or a light meal.
steps: In a bowl, mix chickpea flour with turmeric, red chilli powder, cumin seeds and salt.
Add water gradually and whisk to form a smooth, lump-free batter (consistency of dosa batter).
Stir in finely chopped onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander leaves.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Grease lightly with oil.
Pour a ladle of batter and spread in a circular motion.
Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges. Cook for 2–3 minutes until edges look set.
Flip carefully and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes until golden.
Serve hot with green chutney or curd.

title: Curd Rice (Thayir Sadam)
description: Cooling South Indian comfort food — cooked rice mixed with curd and tempered spices.
steps: Cook rice until very soft (add extra water compared to normal). Let it cool slightly.
Mash the rice lightly with a fork or hand.
Add curd and salt. Mix well. Add a little milk if the mixture feels too thick.
Heat oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds and let splutter.
Add curry leaves, green chilli and a pinch of asafoetida. Stir for 30 seconds.
Pour the tempering over the curd rice and mix well.
Serve at room temperature or slightly chilled. Best eaten the same day.

title: Vegetable Pulao
description: Fragrant one-pot rice dish with mixed vegetables and whole spices.
steps: Wash basmati rice and soak for 20 minutes. Drain.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Add cumin seeds and let splutter.
Add thinly sliced onions and cook until golden, about 6 minutes.
Add minced garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add diced carrot and peas. Stir and cook 2 minutes.
Add turmeric and garam masala. Mix well.
Add the drained rice and gently stir to coat with the spices.
Add 2 cups hot water and salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to lowest setting, cover tightly, and cook 12–15 minutes.
Rest covered for 5 minutes. Fluff gently with a fork and serve.

title: Paneer Bhurji (Scrambled Cottage Cheese)
description: Quick and protein-rich paneer scramble with onions, tomatoes and spices.
steps: Crumble paneer into small pieces with your hands. Set aside.
Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let splutter.
Add finely chopped onions and cook until soft and light golden.
Add minced garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, red chilli powder and salt. Cook until tomatoes are soft.
Add crumbled paneer. Gently mix without mashing too finely.
Cook for 2–3 minutes until paneer is heated through.
Garnish with fresh coriander. Serve with roti or as a wrap filling.

title: Oats Upma
description: A quick and healthy South Indian-style savoury oats dish with vegetables and tempering.
steps: Dry roast oats in a pan for 3–4 minutes until lightly fragrant. Set aside.
Heat oil in the same pan. Add mustard seeds and let splutter.
Add curry leaves and green chilli. Stir 30 seconds.
Add onions and cook until translucent.
Add grated or finely diced carrot. Cook 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric and salt. Cook until soft.
Add 1 cup water and bring to a gentle boil.
Add the roasted oats, stir well to combine.
Cover and cook on low heat for 3–4 minutes until water is absorbed.
Serve hot. Optionally top with lemon juice.

title: Bread Omelette
description: Street-style quick breakfast — fluffy spiced omelette sandwiched between toasted bread.
steps: Beat eggs with salt, turmeric, finely chopped onion, green chilli and coriander.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add butter.
Pour in the egg mixture and spread lightly.
While the omelette is still slightly runny on top, place bread slices on it.
Press gently. Flip the whole thing carefully.
Cook 1 more minute until bread is golden and omelette is fully set.
Slice and serve immediately. Add butter and ketchup to taste.

title: Aloo Sabzi (Spiced Potato Stir-Fry)
description: Simple and satisfying dry potato dish with mustard seeds, turmeric and spices.
steps: Boil or pressure-cook potatoes until just tender. Peel and cut into cubes.
Heat oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and let splutter.
Add curry leaves. Stir for 20 seconds.
Add potato cubes. Toss gently.
Add turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder and salt.
Mix well and cook on medium heat for 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lightly crisp.
Serve with roti, paratha or as a side dish with dal and rice.

title: Tomato Rice
description: Tangy South Indian rice dish cooked with tomatoes and aromatic spices.
steps: Cook rice separately and let it cool slightly (spread on a plate to avoid clumping).
Heat oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds and let splutter.
Add curry leaves and sliced garlic. Stir 30 seconds.
Add chopped onions and cook until golden, about 5 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, red chilli powder and salt.
Cook until tomatoes are fully mushy and oil separates, about 8–10 minutes.
Add cooked rice and gently mix until well coated.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve hot.

title: Masala Omelette
description: Spiced Indian-style omelette — quick protein-rich meal any time of day.
steps: Beat eggs with salt, turmeric, red chilli powder.
Add finely chopped onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander to the egg mixture.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour in the egg mixture and spread into an even circle.
Cook until the bottom is set (about 2 minutes).
Fold in half or serve flat. Serve hot with bread or on its own.

title: Egg Curry (Anda Masala)
description: Boiled eggs simmered in a rich onion-tomato masala gravy.
steps: Hard boil eggs for 10 minutes. Peel and make 2 shallow cuts on each egg. Set aside.
Heat oil in a pan. Add finely chopped onions and cook until deep golden.
Add minced garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and all dry spices. Cook until tomatoes are completely broken down and oil separates.
Add 1 cup water and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add eggs and simmer for 8–10 minutes, spooning gravy over the eggs.
Adjust seasoning. Serve hot with rice or bread.

title: Palak Dal (Spinach Lentil Soup)
description: Nutritious dal made with red lentils and fresh spinach, tempered with cumin and garlic.
steps: Pressure cook red lentils with 1.5 cups water, turmeric and salt until very soft.
Wash spinach and roughly chop. Set aside.
In a pan, heat oil. Add cumin seeds and let splutter.
Add sliced garlic and cook until golden.
Add onions and cook until translucent.
Add tomatoes and red chilli powder. Cook until soft.
Add spinach and cook until wilted, about 3 minutes.
Pour in the cooked lentils and mix well.
Simmer together for 5 minutes. Adjust consistency with water.
Serve hot with rice or roti.

title: Aloo Paratha (Stuffed Potato Flatbread)
description: Whole wheat flatbread stuffed with spiced mashed potato — a classic Indian breakfast.
steps: Mix wheat flour with a pinch of salt and enough water to knead into a soft dough. Cover and rest 20 minutes.
Boil potatoes, peel and mash. Mix with chopped onion, green chilli, coriander, cumin, red chilli powder and salt.
Divide dough into equal balls. Roll out one ball into a small circle.
Place a portion of potato filling in the centre. Bring edges together and seal.
Gently roll out the stuffed ball into a thicker disc.
Cook on a hot tawa (griddle) with a little oil on each side until golden spots appear.
Serve hot with curd or butter.

title: Masala Maggi (Spiced Instant Noodles)
description: Elevated instant noodles with vegetables and extra spices — the classic student meal.
steps: Heat oil. Add cumin seeds. Add onions and cook 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes, green chilli, carrot, peas and turmeric. Cook 3 minutes.
Add 1.5 cups water and bring to a boil.
Add noodle cake and the masala tastemaker packet.
Cook on medium heat for 2 minutes, stirring, until noodles are soft.
Remove from heat while still a little saucy — it thickens quickly.
Serve immediately.

title: Rajma Chawal (Red Kidney Bean Curry with Steamed Rice)
description: Classic North Indian comfort food: tender red kidney beans slow-cooked in a rich onion-tomato gravy, served over hot basmati rice.
steps: Soak kidney beans overnight for 8 hours. Pressure cook with 3 cups water and salt for 15 minutes until soft.
Cook basmati rice with 2 cups water until fluffy; set aside.
Heat oil in a pan. Add cumin seeds and let splutter.
Add finely chopped onions, minced ginger, and garlic. Sauté until deep golden brown.
Add pureed tomatoes, turmeric, chilli powder, and coriander powder. Cook until oil separates.
Add cooked kidney beans with their cooking water. Simmer on medium-low for 15-20 minutes, lightly mashing some beans to thicken gravy.
Finish with garam masala and fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Chana Masala (Spiced Chickpea Curry)
description: A flavorful, tangy chickpea curry simmered in a spiced onion-tomato gravy with warm spices.
steps: Soak chickpeas overnight. Boil or pressure cook with water and salt until tender.
Heat oil in a kadai. Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle.
Add finely chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add minced ginger, garlic, and chopped green chilli. Fry for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, coriander powder, and salt. Cook until tomatoes are mushy.
Add boiled chickpeas and 1 cup of water. Simmer on low for 10-15 minutes.
Stir in garam masala and lemon juice. Garnish with coriander leaves.

title: Paneer Butter Masala (Cottage Cheese in Rich Tomato Makhani Gravy)
description: Restaurant-style cottage cheese cubes bathed in a velvety, mildly spiced creamy tomato gravy with butter and aromatic fenugreek.
steps: Boil chopped tomatoes, onions, ginger, and garlic in 1 cup water for 10 minutes until soft. Cool and blend into a smooth puree.
Strain puree through a fine sieve for a silky restaurant texture.
Heat butter and oil in a pan. Add red chilli powder on low flame for vibrant color.
Pour in the strained tomato gravy. Simmer for 10-12 minutes until oil surfaces.
Add salt, garam masala, and crushed kasuri methi.
Gently slide in fresh paneer cubes and simmer for 3 minutes.
Swirl in fresh cream and serve hot with naan or jeera rice.

title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
description: Tender marinated chicken chunks simmered in a spiced, buttery and velvety tomato cream sauce.
steps: Marinate chicken pieces in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chilli powder, and salt for 20 minutes.
Pan-sear the chicken pieces in oil over high heat until browned (about 6-8 minutes). Set aside.
Cook onions, tomatoes, ginger, and garlic in butter. Puree until silky smooth.
Return gravy to the pan. Add chilli powder, garam masala, and salt. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add the seared chicken into the sauce and simmer for 8 minutes until cooked through.
Stir in fresh cream and crushed kasuri methi. Serve with hot butter naan.

title: Homestyle Chicken Curry (Tariwala Chicken)
description: A comforting everyday chicken curry cooked with onions, tomatoes, ginger, garlic, and freshly roasted Indian spices.
steps: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Crackle cumin seeds.
Add finely chopped onions and sauté until nicely browned, about 8 minutes.
Add crushed ginger, garlic, and slit chillies. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and dry spices (turmeric, coriander, chilli powder, salt). Cook until oil releases.
Add chicken pieces and sear in the masala on high heat for 5 minutes.
Add 1.5 cups water, cover with lid, and simmer on medium heat for 20 minutes until chicken is tender.
Sprinkle garam masala and chopped coriander leaves before serving.

title: Masala Dosa (Crispy Rice Crepe with Spiced Potato Bhaji)
description: Golden, crisp fermented rice and lentil crepe stuffed with aromatic turmeric spiced mashed potato filling.
steps: Boil and coarsely mash potatoes.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, and green chillies.
Add sliced onions and cook till translucent, then add turmeric and salt.
Toss in mashed potatoes with 2 tbsp water to create a soft, spreadable filling.
Heat a flat cast iron tawa, pour a ladle of dosa batter and spread thinly in concentric circles.
Drizzle oil around edges until the crepe turns golden and crisp.
Place potato masala in the center, fold, and serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.

title: South Indian Sambar (Lentil & Mixed Vegetable Stew)
description: A nutritious, tangy South Indian lentil and vegetable stew spiced with tamarind and freshly roasted sambar powder.
steps: Pressure cook toor dal with water and turmeric until mushy; whisk smooth.
Extract tamarind juice in 1 cup warm water.
Boil vegetables in tamarind water with salt and turmeric until tender.
Add sambar powder and simmer for 5 minutes until raw spice aroma fades.
Pour in cooked mashed dal, adjust consistency with water, and bring to a gentle boil.
In a small pan, temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, and dried chillies in oil; pour over hot sambar.

title: Lemon Rice (Chitranna / South Indian Tempered Rice)
description: Bright yellow, tangy tempered rice with peanuts, curry leaves, mustard seeds, and freshly squeezed lemon juice.
steps: Cook rice and spread on a wide plate to cool so grains remain separate.
Heat oil in a pan. Fry peanuts until crisp and golden; push to the side.
Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, minced ginger, and slit chillies.
Turn off flame, add turmeric powder and salt to hot oil.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice into the tempering.
Gently fold into the cooled rice until evenly golden yellow and fragrant.

title: Chicken Dum Biryani (Fragrant Layered Basmati Rice)
description: Royal Mughlai one-pot feast featuring tender marinated chicken, fragrant saffron basmati rice, caramelized onions, and fresh mint.
steps: Marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala, turmeric, and salt for 30 minutes.
Deep fry sliced onions in oil until dark golden (birista); drain.
Parboil basmati rice with whole spices in boiling salted water until 70% cooked (about 6 minutes); drain.
In a heavy pot, cook marinated chicken with ghee until 80% tender.
Layer parboiled rice over the chicken. Scatter fried onions, chopped mint, and coriander.
Drizzle melted ghee, cover with tight lid, and steam on lowest flame (dum) for 15 minutes.
Gently fluff from the bottom to preserve layers. Serve hot with raita.

title: Dal Tadka (Yellow Lentil Soup with Ghee Tempering)
description: Smooth yellow lentils simmered with turmeric and garlic, finished with a smoking ghee tempering of cumin, dried red chillies, and garlic.
steps: Pressure cook toor and moong dal with turmeric, salt, and water until very soft (about 4 whistles).
Whisk the dal lightly to achieve a smooth consistency.
Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a pan. Add onions, ginger, and chopped tomatoes; sauté until mushy.
Pour in boiled dal and simmer for 5 minutes. Adjust water as needed.
In a small tadka pan, heat remaining ghee until hot. Add cumin seeds and sliced garlic; fry until golden.
Add a pinch of red chilli powder and pour sizzling tadka immediately over the dal.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve with hot rotis or rice.

title: Palak Paneer (Cottage Cheese in Pureed Spinach Gravy)
description: Wholesome fresh spinach blanched and pureed with garlic and mild spices, gently folded with soft cottage cheese cubes.
steps: Blanch spinach leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, then immediately plunge into ice-cold water to retain bright green color.
Blend blanched spinach with green chillies into a smooth puree.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, minced garlic, ginger, and chopped onions; fry until translucent.
Add chopped tomato and salt. Cook until soft.
Pour in the spinach puree and simmer gently for 5 minutes on low heat.
Add garam masala and slide in paneer cubes. Cook for 2 minutes so paneer absorbs the gravy.
Finish with a splash of cream and serve hot.

title: Pav Bhaji (Spiced Mashed Vegetable Curry with Buttered Buns)
description: Famous Mumbai street food: buttery, spiced mashed mixed vegetables served with golden toasted pav buns and lemon wedges.
steps: Boil potatoes, cauliflower, and peas until very soft. Mash thoroughly.
Melt 2 tbsp butter on a wide tawa or pan. Sauté chopped onions and capsicum until fragrant.
Add chopped tomatoes, pav bhaji masala, red chilli powder, and salt. Cook until mushy and butter separates.
Add the mashed boiled vegetables with 1/2 cup water. Mash continuously with a potato masher while simmering.
Simmer for 10 minutes, adjusting butter and water for a silky, rich consistency.
Slit pav buns and toast on tawa with generous butter.
Serve bhaji hot with dollop of butter, chopped onions, and lemon wedges.

title: Chole Bhature (Punjabi Spiced Chickpeas with Fried Puffy Bread)
description: Iconic North Indian specialty: dark, aromatic spiced chickpeas cooked with dried amla and whole spices, paired with hot, fluffy fried bhature.
steps: Boil soaked chickpeas with a tea bag and salt to achieve deep dark brown color.
Knead flour with yogurt and a pinch of baking powder; let dough rest 2 hours.
In hot oil, sauté finely chopped onions, ginger, and garlic until golden brown.
Add pureed tomatoes, coriander powder, amchur, and chole masala; cook till oil floats.
Add boiled chickpeas, lightly mash a few to thicken, and simmer 15 minutes.
Roll out dough portions and deep fry in hot oil until puffed and golden.
Serve piping hot chole with puffed bhature, pickled onions, and green chillies.

title: Kadai Paneer (Bell Pepper & Cottage Cheese Stir-Fry)
description: Succulent cottage cheese cubes and crunchy bell peppers tossed in a robust, freshly ground kadai spice masala with tomatoes.
steps: Dry roast coriander seeds, cumin seeds, and dry red chillies; crush coarsely into kadai masala.
Dice onions and capsicum into squares.
Heat oil in a kadai. Add minced ginger and garlic, then add pureed tomatoes and salt. Cook until thick.
Add crushed kadai masala and sauté for 2 minutes.
In a separate pan, quickly blister diced capsicum and onions in 1 tsp oil on high heat so they remain crunchy.
Combine vegetables and paneer cubes into the tomato masala; toss gently on medium heat for 3 minutes.
Garnish with julienned ginger and fresh coriander leaves.

title: Jeera Rice (Fragrant Cumin-Spiced Basmati Rice)
description: Long-grain basmati rice cooked with whole cumin seeds, ghee, and aromatic cloves for the perfect curry accompaniment.
steps: Wash basmati rice until water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes; drain.
Heat ghee in a pot on medium flame. Add cumin seeds, cloves, and cardamom pods.
Let cumin crackle and release its nutty fragrance (do not burn).
Add drained rice and gently sauté for 1 minute so grains are coated in aromatic ghee.
Pour in 2 cups of hot water and salt. Bring to a rolling boil.
Cover with tight-fitting lid, lower flame to lowest setting, and cook undisturbed for 10 minutes.
Turn off heat, let rest for 5 minutes, and fluff gently with a fork.

title: Dal Makhani (Slow-Cooked Creamy Black Lentil Stew)
description: Whole black lentils and kidney beans slow-simmered overnight with butter, fresh cream, and subtle Kashmiri spices.
steps: Soak black lentils and kidney beans overnight. Pressure cook with salt and water until completely tender.
In a heavy pot, heat 1 tbsp butter, add minced ginger-garlic and tomato puree. Cook until butter separates.
Add red chilli powder and salt.
Pour in the cooked lentils along with their broth. Mash lightly with the back of a ladle.
Simmer on very low heat for at least 30-45 minutes, stirring periodically to develop rich creaminess.
Stir in remaining butter, fresh cream, and crushed kasuri methi.
Serve rich and hot with garlic naan or steamed rice.

title: Baingan Bharta (Smoky Roasted Eggplant Mash)
description: Whole eggplant roasted directly on open flame for a rustic smoky char, mashed and sautéed with onions, green chillies, and tomatoes.
steps: Slit eggplant and insert garlic cloves inside. Roast over open flame turning until skin is completely charred and flesh is tender.
Cover in a bowl for 5 minutes, peel off charred skin, and mash the pulp thoroughly.
Heat mustard oil in a pan until hot. Add chopped onions and ginger; fry till golden.
Add chopped tomatoes, green chillies, turmeric, chilli powder, and salt. Cook till soft.
Add mashed roasted eggplant. Cook on medium-high heat for 7-8 minutes, stirring continuously.
Garnish with abundant fresh coriander leaves and serve with hot phulkas.

title: Rice Kheer (Creamy Cardamom & Nut Rice Pudding)
description: Traditional Indian festival dessert: fragrant basmati rice slow-simmered in whole milk with green cardamom, saffron, and slivered almonds.
steps: Wash rice and soak in water for 15 minutes; drain and crush coarsely with fingers.
Bring milk to a boil in a heavy pot, then lower flame to simmer.
Add crushed rice to milk and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes, stirring frequently so it doesn’t stick.
When rice is completely soft and milk has thickened to a creamy consistency, stir in sugar.
Cook for another 5 minutes until sugar dissolves.
Add crushed cardamom powder and toasted nuts.
Serve warm or chilled.
